text.p: These are the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The United Nations-sponsored talks between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities on Cyprus are due to start today, and until they end on July 13 a full media blackout will prevail.
- Greece's Costas Simitis and Turkey's Suleyman Demirel reach a surprise non-aggression pact on the sidelines of the NATO conference in Madrid.
- New incentives are promised for the Cyprus stock exchange as it faces an uncertain future.
- The United Nations report some progress on the indirect military dialogue aimed at reducing tension between the two sides along the ceasefire line.

- A new investment bond, the Carrington Holiday Investment Bond, is due to be launched in Cyprus next month, allowing holders to enjoy vacations at participating hotels or resorts at once-only fixed prices.
- Burger war shifts to Larnaca. Greek chain Goodys plans to open up its second Cyprus store in Larnaca - right next to McDonalds.
- The UN talks on Cyprus will start amid a news blackout.
- The government will give its counter proposals to civil service doctors today on their demands for revised pay structures and pension benefits.
- The UN talks start today in the dark, and without any particular expectations.
- In a surprise development, Costas Simitis and Suleyman Demirel agree in principle that Greece and Turkey should strive to solve their differences in a peaceful manner.
- The Madrid accord between Greece and Turkey could have an impact on the talks scheduled to start today on Cyprus at Troutbeck in New York.
- A new round of talks between the two sides is scheduled to start in August.
